passage: In the colony park in Ludhiana, Gurleen climbed the low slide while her mother Minakshi sat on the bench. Halfway up, Gurleen looked back. Minakshi waved. Gurleen slid down, tripped on the grass and scraped her palm. She ran straight to the bench, holding her hand out. Minakshi blew on it and held her until the crying stopped. Then Gurleen slipped off her lap and ran back to the slide, glancing once at the bench.

qa.q: Where was Minakshi sitting while Gurleen played?
qa.a: Minakshi sat on the bench in the colony park.

qa.q: Why did Gurleen look back at the bench halfway up the slide?
qa.a: She wanted to check that her mother was still there, and seeing Minakshi wave made her feel safe to keep going.

qa.q: How does Minakshi's steady presence support Gurleen's play?
qa.a: Because Minakshi stays in view and comforts her quickly when she is hurt, Gurleen feels secure enough to go back and explore on her own.

qa.q: What would change if Minakshi often walked away without Gurleen knowing?
qa.a: Gurleen might stop exploring and cling instead, because she could no longer count on her mother being there when she needed her.

grounding: Shows a toddler's trust that her caregiver will be there to meet her needs, which lets her explore.

passage:
"Mama?" Varun's voice came from the cot in the dark.
"I'm here, jaan," said Salma, turning on the small lamp.
"Milk."
"Milk is coming. Let me warm it."
Varun sat up, holding the cot bars, and watched the door. He didn't cry.
"Here it is." She sat on the floor beside him while he drank.
"Mama stay."
"I'll stay till you're sleepy."
He handed back the cup, lay down and curled his fingers round her thumb.

qa.q: What did Varun ask for when he woke?
qa.a: He asked for milk.

qa.q: Why didn't Varun cry while waiting for the milk?
qa.a: He seems sure from experience that when Salma says milk is coming, it really will come, so he can wait calmly.

qa.q: What in Salma's replies builds Varun's sense of security?
qa.a: She answers him right away, tells him exactly what will happen and then does it, so her words and actions match.

qa.q: What might Salma feel as Varun curls his fingers round her thumb?
qa.a: She would likely feel tired but tender, knowing her steady care is what lets him settle back to sleep. ❤️

grounding: Illustrates a toddler's secure trust that his caregiver will meet his physical and emotional needs.

passage:
Monthly note on Payal, from Asif at the day-care.
When Payal joined in June, she screamed at drop-off and wouldn't let me hold her. I kept to the same steps every day: greet her at the gate, offer her the blue cushion, snack after circle time.
By now she waves bye to her father and toddles in. When she's hungry, she comes and taps the snack shelf, then waits. Yesterday she fell asleep on my arm during story. 😊

qa.q: What did Payal do at drop-off when she first joined in June?
qa.a: She screamed at drop-off and wouldn't let Asif hold her.

qa.q: What does Payal tapping the snack shelf and then waiting suggest she believes?
qa.a: It suggests she now believes Asif will notice and give her food, so she trusts her need will be met without crying.

qa.q: Which of Asif's habits helped Payal settle in?
qa.a: Doing the same steps every day, from greeting her at the gate to snack after circle time, made the day predictable and let her trust Asif.

qa.q: How might Payal's father feel reading this note?
qa.a: He would likely feel relieved and grateful that she has gone from screaming at drop-off to waving bye and resting on Asif's arm. 🙏

grounding: Shows a toddler building secure trust that a consistent caregiver will meet her needs.

passage: In the wheat field's shade, Amandeep woke from his nap on the charpai and called out, 'Ammi!' Dilnaz, cutting grass nearby, straightened and waved. 'Here, jaan.' He sat up, sucked his thumb, and watched her. When a buffalo lowed, he called again, and again she answered and came to rub his back. Soon he climbed down and lined up pebbles, glancing now and then to find her still there.

qa.q: What was Dilnaz doing when Amandeep woke?
qa.a: She was cutting grass nearby in the field.

qa.q: Why did Amandeep keep glancing at Dilnaz while he played?
qa.a: He wanted to check she was still there; knowing she would answer made him feel safe enough to play.

qa.q: What does Dilnaz's response show about building trust?
qa.a: Answering every call, even small ones, teaches him that his needs will be met, which lets him explore on his own.

qa.q: What would change if Dilnaz often ignored his calls?
qa.a: He might cling more or cry longer, because he could not be sure she would come when he needed her.

grounding: Illustrates a toddler's growing sense of security from a caregiver who responds consistently.

passage: At two in the morning, rain drummed on the flat's window in Hamburg. Hiroshi woke up and cried. Within a minute Elif was at the cot, her hair messy. 'I'm here. Just rain.' She laid a warm hand on his tummy. He hiccupped, found her finger and gripped it. His eyes closed slowly. Elif stayed a while, then tiptoed out. Hiroshi stirred once, then went back to sleep.

qa.q: What woke Hiroshi at two in the morning?
qa.a: Rain drumming on the window woke him, and he cried.

qa.q: What does Hiroshi gripping Elif's finger suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: It suggests he felt comforted and safe with her there, and could relax back into sleep.

qa.q: What is helpful about how Elif responded?
qa.a: She came quickly and calmly and used touch and a few soft words, which is a steady, predictable comfort.

qa.q: What is it like for Elif to get up for these wakings?
qa.a: It may be tiring for her, but she seems to accept it and still stays until he settles. 😴

grounding: Shows a toddler feeling secure because a caregiver reliably meets his needs at night, set in Germany.
